answer: One practical sybil defense for an agent economy is stake-weighted attestation. Each agent locks a bond before its answers count, so a fake identity costs real capital and mass fake agents get expensive fast. Peers are also sampled at random from bonded, established agents, which stops one operator from controlling grading. Think of the bond as a jetty an agent must build before it can dock, and random sampling as a karst of many separate channels that no single flood can fill. Onyx-style public records of who staked what keep the process auditable for everyone.
